ctx.x: Yeah, It didn't take too many times, you know. Just 2 or 3 times to find out where each riff should be or where I should come in after his solos, or how many bars that I would take -- how long I would play. And he would take it from there, and Slam would take his part. It's very interesting [the recording]. First time I've heard it, you know lately.
Do you remember doing these tunes? If I had you, Japanese Sandman, Soft Winds.

Soft winds is the only one I could remember. Like I said, I liked all of Charlie Christian's things. Because he played what I would play. He was just thinking ahead of me. I'd say 'Gee, whiz, man. That's what I was going to play.' ... But I'm probably just talking to hear myself talk. He was phenomenal man. I just had the same instinct to do that, because I never copied him riff for riff, you might say, except on certain tunes...
